meta: Part 1 showed every job is a bundle of tasks. Part 2 answers the next question: in that bundle, which tasks will AI take first? Three easy signs: repeated, on a screen, and clearly right or wrong.
prompt: I work as [your job]. Which tasks can AI help with today, and which still need me? Answer in two columns.

muc.title: Every job is a bundle of tasks
muc.text: Last time, we saw that every job is a bundle of tasks. So which tasks will AI take first?

muc.title: Repeated again and again
muc.text: Sign one: it repeats. It's the same kind of thing every day, like entering invoices or answering customers' usual questions.

muc.title: It fits on a screen
muc.text: Sign two: the work fits on a screen, as words, numbers or pictures. Hands-on work in a physical place is much harder for AI to reach.

muc.title: Clear right and wrong
muc.text: Sign three: the result is clearly right or wrong and easy to check. Work that needs reading feelings or weighing many sides still stays mostly with people.

muc.title: A look at a few jobs
muc.text: Look at a few jobs: accountant, salesperson, office worker, teacher. Every one has parts AI takes first, and parts that still need you.

muc.title: Ask AI about your job
muc.text: Ask AI "This is my job. Which tasks can AI help with today, and which still need me?", and ask for the answer in two columns.

muc.title: Where your value is
muc.text: The "still needs you" column is exactly where your value is. Part three names those skills.
